correctness.rationale: C: The conditional law follows from differentiating the constant stationary expectation of \(G(x(t))\) and using arbitrary continuous derivatives on the compact current-state range. The mean balance then defines a size-biased law. The exact rational defect is a pointwise algebraic decomposition after the reciprocal balance, and the variance/activity identity follows from the conditional covariance plus equality of the current and delayed marginals. Equality cases force \(X=x_*\) or \(\dot x=0\) almost surely and therefore the constant positive equilibrium. The bundled checker replayed the two nontrivial algebraic reductions and returned ALGEBRA_OK. No finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: V: The Mackey–Glass equation is a canonical delayed-chaos benchmark whose literature focuses heavily on bifurcations, attractors and prediction. The new identity gives an exact, delay-independent one-time marginal diagnostic: a non-equilibrium stationary state must carry a strictly positive size-biased high-moment excess above the positive-equilibrium scale, with an explicit squared remainder. The activity budget independently converts a marginal production-variance surplus into exact mean-square temporal activity. These are reproducible constraints useful for validating simulated or empirical stationary regimes and for distinguishing equilibrium from recurrent dynamics; they are not merely a renamed parameter substitution from the prior Nicholson or Hutchinson–Wright statements.
